briefdescription.para: Implementation for databaseconnectionpool: Opens one pqxx connection using the configured credentials and a connect timeout.

detaileddescription.para: This file implements the pool's lifecycle. createDatabaseConnection() opens and validates a single connection; the constructor spins up all slots in parallel with retries; get_connection()/return_connection() lease and return links, measuring waits and throttling saturation warnings; reconnect_all() repairs every idle link in parallel while holding the pool lock so nothing is handed out half-reconnected.

WHY THIS FILE MATTERS IN THE SERVER: This is where the server decides how many database connections exist and what happens when they are all busy. It translates configuration (DB_MAX_CONN, DB_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_MS) into real behaviour, maps a wait that expires to a DatabaseBusy exception (which the HTTP layer answers with 503), and cooperates with the watchdog to recover from database restarts. Without it there would be no connection reuse, no back-pressure, and no automatic recovery.

CONCEPTS TO LEARN (for beginners):
std::async and std::future (run work in parallel and collect its result): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/thread/async
std::future::get and wait: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/thread/future
std::atomic::compare_exchange_strong (an atomic "update if unchanged"): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/atomic/atomic/compare_exchange
std::chrono::steady_clock (a monotonic clock ideal for timeouts): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/chrono/steady_clock
Exponential backoff (sleep longer after each failed attempt)
exit() and EXIT_FAILURE from the C standard library: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/program/exit
